vo: Now the fun part. Start a new group chat and add all five Bots.
Send one message: everyone post your most important finding, then turn it into one plan with today's top five moves.
The replies come in. The Store Bot reports that hiking packs are running low.
And the Content Bot answers on its own: hold the hiking pack video until the restock is confirmed.
Nobody told it to. It simply saw the store report in the same thread.
Then the Chief joins everything into one plan: five moves, in order, with the hiking pack video safely on hold.
And tomorrow you don't even send a message. At eight, the plan is simply there, waiting for your yes.
By Friday the team has checked the store every morning, written six report cards, planned a week of content and scored a list of leads. You approved each one in seconds.
The old way: five tools every morning, stock checked by hand, evenings lost to client reports. The new way: one plan, waiting in one chat.
Add it up, and that's hours back every week, spent on the work only you can do.
You stop being the glue. You become the boss who says yes or no.
One. Build the head first. Without a chief, five Bots are just five more chats.
Two. Give every Bot one job and one schedule. Small and clear beats big and vague.
Three, and this is the one that breaks everything: never switch on real sending on day one. Start with sample data and drafts only, and go live after a week of good results.
Head, two arms, chest, legs, and a shield. Build it one piece at a time, and let your Bots check each other's work.
So start with the head today. One Bot, one message, and tomorrow morning you'll read your first brief.
